widgetMetadata.instructions: Each entry under `widgets` describes one chart/widget rendered on this page of the Israeli Ecosystem dashboard. Descriptions are result-agnostic: they explain what the visualization shows and how to interpret it, not the specific numbers. The `dataPaths` array on each entry lists dot-notation paths inside this same JSON file where the underlying data for that widget lives (e.g. "kpis.patentingStartups" or "ipIntensity.items") When summarizing or answering questions about a number from this snapshot, locate the relevant widget(s) by `dataPaths` and quote the corresponding `description` to explain the metric. Widgets that have a 10 year trend usually show the total overall (across all years) and you get the exact data for each year in the past 10 years. The 10 year data do not add up to the total of course

angels:kpi-angels.title: Angels
angels:kpi-angels.description: Total number of individuals identified as angel investors in the Israeli startup population. The sparkline shows how many wrote their first ever recorded check in each of the last ten years, so it tracks new entrants rather than everyone active in a year.

angels:kpi-investments.title: Investments
angels:kpi-investments.description: Total angel-company pairings, counting each company once per angel however many rounds they joined. The bars show investments per year, where the solid portion was made by angels writing their first ever check and the outline above it is repeat activity from angels already in the data.

angels:kpi-companies.title: Companies Backed
angels:kpi-companies.description: Distinct companies in the Israeli startup population with at least one identified angel behind them. The sparkline counts companies receiving their first angel check each year, so a company appears once however many angels back it later.

angels:kpi-age.title: Age at First Check
angels:kpi-age.description: How old angels were when they made their first recorded investment, in five-year bands from 25 with an open final band. The source carries no birth date, so age is reconstructed from a person’s age when they founded a company against that company’s founding year, which means it only exists for angels who are also founders. The covered share is stated on the card.

angels:kpi-exit-lag.title: Exit to First Check
angels:kpi-exit-lag.description: How many years passed between a founder exit and that person’s first angel investment, in two-year bands with an open final band and the median called out. The population is only angels who founded a company that was acquired or went public, and the covered count against that population is stated on the card. Angels whose first check predates their exit fall outside the measured set.

angels:profile.title: Startup Experience
angels:profile.description: What these people did before they started writing checks. The donut splits every angel into three tiers by founder background — never founded a company, founded but no exit, founded and exited. The centre of the donut reads the founded share at rest, and on hover names the tier under the cursor and gives the mean number of investments per angel in it, which is what shows whether founding and exiting changes how much someone invests. The exited tier is deliberately not split by whether investing started before or after the exit, because that split key correlates with portfolio size and the comparison would be circular; the count of angels already investing before their exit is carried in the data as a note.

angels:dna.title: Angel DNA
angels:dna.description: The share of angels with a technical versus a non-technical background, over the angels with a known classification. Same technical / non-technical axis the founders page uses, so the two are comparable. Technical means an affirmatively technical background; non-technical is everyone else, not a named function.

angels:geography.title: Where Angels Are Based
angels:geography.description: Where the angels backing Israeli startups are located, split into Israel, the United States and the rest of the world, with the angel count, the mean investments per angel and the number of companies each group reaches. Country aliases are folded together first. Angels with no recorded country are excluded from the split rather than folded into the rest, because a missing country could be either, and are reported separately in the data. A large share sit outside Israel, which is diaspora and foreign capital reaching Israeli companies.

angels:employers.title: Where Angels Worked
angels:employers.description: The most common prior employers among angels, counted once per person per employer. A person’s own founder roles are excluded, schools are excluded so they cannot leak in from the employer side, and membership networks and advisory councils are excluded as affiliations rather than jobs. Built like the founders page equivalent, so the two are comparable.

angels:schools.title: Where Angels Studied
angels:schools.description: The most common institutions angels attended, counted once per person per school. Shares are against the angels with a recorded school rather than all angels. Built like the founders page equivalent, so the two are comparable.

angels:gender.title: Gender
angels:gender.description: The gender split among identified angels, over the angels with a known value. This became reportable only after an enrichment backfill took coverage from roughly 45% to 99%; before that the field was populated for angels who are also founders and almost nobody else. The share of women here runs below the equivalent share among founders.

angels:leaderboard.title: Most Active Angels
angels:leaderboard.description: Angels ranked by how many distinct companies in the Israeli startup population they backed. Bars are scaled to the top angel. Each row shows the portfolio count and the span of years between the first and most recent recorded round, with a marker for angels who founded a company that exited. Hovering a row names the companies they founded and the most recent companies they backed. Follow-on rounds into the same company count once toward the portfolio, so the round count can exceed it.

angels:portfolio-distribution.title: Investments per Angel
angels:portfolio-distribution.description: How concentrated angel activity is: the number of angels who made 1, 2, 3-4, 5-9, or 10 or more investments, with the share of all investments each group accounts for. Reads as a power law, where most identified angels appear once and a small group carries a disproportionate share of the deals.

angels:stage-mix.title: Where Angels Enter
angels:stage-mix.description: The funding stage of every equity round an angel participated in, drawn as a centred funnel read top to bottom in ladder order, from pre-seed through seed and up. Rounds labelled Angel are counted as pre-seed: the two are one rung under two names, and the evidence is that they almost never appear at the same company, that neither consistently precedes the other when they do, that both sit about the same distance before that company own seed round, that the same investors write both, and that Angel was the common label until roughly 2016 and pre-seed has been the common label since. Band width and fill depth both carry the number of rounds. SAFEs, convertible notes and bridges are financing instruments rather than stages, so they are grouped under Other instead of being folded into a seed bucket; Other has no place on a ladder and is left off the chart, though it stays in the data. A round with several identified angels counts once per angel.

angels:sectors.title: Where Angels Invest
angels:sectors.description: Angel-backed companies grouped by subindustry, drawn as a circle-pack bubble chart: each bubble is a subindustry sized by how many angel investments went into it and colored by its parent industry. Counted at the angel-company pair level, so a company backed by three angels contributes three. Hovering a bubble shows that subindustry’s share of all angel investments, angels and backed companies, plus outcomes for those companies: the median total they have raised (over the ones that disclose funding) and how many reached a completed acquisition or listing. Colors match the industry palette used across the dashboard.

angels:coverage.title: Coverage
angels:coverage.description: How much of the Israeli startup population has an identified angel behind it. Angel names in the source data are raw strings, and only the ones that resolve to a real person are counted here, so roughly half the individual investor names in the source are not represented. Every number on this page is therefore a floor rather than a complete count of Israeli angel activity.
